input.quote: 13.1 IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale: Direction check: every licence grant in this deal runs from us as licensor to MSL (§ 13.3(a) royalty-free confidential-information licence at p0208; Equipment and Program Loan Agreement §§ 5-6 at p1530/p1532; Attachment 6/Appendix A restrictions at p1301/p1337/p1346), so those grants benefit our side and are not flagged. On the inbound side we take something stronger than a licence: § 13.1-13.2 give IBM outright ownership and an assignment of all IP in hardware, software, design and documentation of Products, plus MSL inventions on Products and IBM processes, with MSL retaining only a use-right for performing its own obligations here. Ownership is inherently perpetual and irrevocable, is not revocable at MSL's discretion, and is freely transferable to successors and usable by our contractors; "IBM" is defined at § 1.9 as "International Business Machines Corporation, Armonk, New York, USA, and its Subsidiaries", so affiliate coverage is automatic and no separate affiliate/written-notice mechanic is needed. The preferred position is therefore met (indeed exceeded) on its material terms. Two non-material points noted only: § 24.1 records that "MSL conveys to IBM no software title or license under the intellectual property rights of MSL or of any third party", and there is no express standing licence to MSL background IP - but that residual exposure is contained because MSL "shall not use any proprietary processes for the assembly, subassembly and final tests, and quality testing of the Products" without written agreement, and § 24.1(b) leaves a consent path. These are rationale observations, not fallback failures, so no redline is proposed.
